prompt: Match each Key Vault object to what an application does with it.
hint: Handed out, or used in place?

pairs.right: Asks the vault to sign with it
Has it renewed with an authority

prompt: Why is a key safer than a secret against a compromised application?
hint: Where does the private part live?

choices.text: Keys are encrypted and secrets are not
choices.why: Both are protected at rest; the difference is what leaves the vault.

choices.text: The key never leaves the vault
choices.why: Right. The app gets signatures, not the key.

choices.text: Keys expire automatically every day
choices.why: Expiry is a policy; the shop's is a year.

choices.text: Only premium vaults hold secrets
choices.why: Every tier holds secrets.

prompt: An attacker with an administrator account deletes the shop's vault. With purge protection on, what can they not do?

choices.text: Delete the vault
choices.why: Deletion still works; soft delete keeps it recoverable.

choices.text: Read the secrets before deleting it
choices.why: Purge protection does not govern reading; roles do.

choices.text: Purge it before the 90 days pass
choices.why: Right. Nobody can purge, not even an Owner.

choices.text: Turn soft delete off
choices.why: That cannot be done on new vaults anyway; purge is what is blocked.

prompt: Why does the vault use `enableRbacAuthorization: true`?

choices.text: Access policies cannot grant read access
choices.why: They can; the issue is having a second system.

choices.text: One permission system, not two
choices.why: Right. One system to review instead of two.

choices.text: RBAC makes the vault public
choices.why: Network access is a separate setting, and it is Disabled.

choices.text: It is required for purge protection
choices.why: The two settings are independent.

prompt: What can the app's identity do with the role *Key Vault Secrets User* on kv-shop-prod?

choices.text: Read and write secrets
choices.why: Writing needs a different role.

choices.text: Read secrets in every vault of the subscription
choices.why: The assignment's scope is this one vault.

choices.text: Read secret values in this vault
choices.why: Right. Nothing more, and nowhere else.

choices.text: Grant itself more roles
choices.why: That needs a role that manages access, which this is not.

prompt: The linter's warning on leaky.bicep goes away once `@secure()` is added. Why does the shop still not set secrets in Bicep?
hint: Where was the value before it reached the template?

choices.text: Bicep cannot create secrets
choices.why: It can, as leaky.bicep shows.

choices.text: @secure() stores the value in the deployment history
choices.why: It keeps it out of the history.

choices.text: The value travelled to get there
choices.why: Right. The template sets up the vault and access; values are set apart.

choices.text: Secrets set by Bicep never expire
choices.why: Expiry does not depend on what set the value.

prompt: An app setting that names a secret starts with @Microsoft.___( .
hint: The service's name, as one word.

prompt: Why does `DefaultAzureCredential` let the same code run on a laptop and in production?
hint: It tries ways in a fixed order.

choices.text: It finds whichever identity is there
choices.why: Right. Managed identity in Azure, the CLI sign-in on a laptop.

choices.text: It stores a credential in the code
choices.why: It stores none; that is the point.

choices.text: It skips authentication on laptops
choices.why: It authenticates as the developer signed in to the CLI.

choices.text: It reads the connection string from the vault
choices.why: It needs an identity before it can read anything.

prompt: The app fetches payments-api-key from the vault on every request and starts failing on Black Friday. What happened?

choices.text: The key expired that morning
choices.why: Nothing in the story says so; the pattern is the busiest day.

choices.text: It hit the vault's limits on requests per vault
choices.why: Right. Read once and cache.

choices.text: Black Friday disables managed identities
choices.why: Nothing disables identities by date.

choices.text: The reference resolved to an old version
choices.why: The app reads in code here, and an old version would still work.

prompt: Put the steps of rotating the database password in the safe order.
hint: The database must accept it before anyone fetches it.
items: The vault publishes a near-expiry event
A function generates a new password
The function sets it on the database
The function writes it to the vault as a new version
The app picks up the latest version
trap: Writing to the vault before the database is the slip: the app would fetch a password the database does not accept yet.

prompt: How many days before expiry does the receipt-signing key rotate?
Which answer does the shop prefer for the database's password, where the service allows it?
hint: Remove the thing that needs rotating.

choices.text: Rotating it every week instead of every year
choices.why: Faster rotation still leaves a password.

choices.text: Storing it as a key instead of a secret
choices.why: A password is a value to hand out, which is what a secret is.

choices.text: A managed identity, with Entra sign-in
choices.why: Right. No password, and so no rotation.

choices.text: Writing it in the app's settings directly
choices.why: That puts the value where anyone with read on the app sees it.
